@danwinship So it turns out CNO uses `controllercmd.NewControllerCommandConfig`

https://github.com/openshift/cluster-network-operator/blob/6dc18040e7c214f6a1db25b6f5ef4642c6c6a186/cmd/cluster-network-operator/main.go#L49-L51

which automatically sets up an HTTPS metrics server but with hard-coded TLS min version (TLS 1.2) and cipher suites, which, of course, isn't TLS profile compliant. I missed that before. It also does not (directly) provide a way to customize the TLS config, although it seems there is a clunky way to do it. Assuming that's true, we'll also need to watch for TLS profile changes and restart the process (there's no way to hot-reload the metrics server). Given that, the changes I made to the `ReconcileOperConfig` controller to watch the `APIServer` (and `HostedCluster` for hypershift) would basically move to a higher-level and trigger process restart.

Other options are:
- use plain HTTP for operator metrics
- continue to use the hard-coded TLS  defaults and don't honor the centralized TLS profile for operator metrics

but I assume neither of those is acceptable.

> So it turns out CNO uses `controllercmd.NewControllerCommandConfig` ...
which automatically sets up an HTTPS metrics server but with hard-coded TLS min version (TLS 1.2) and cipher suites, which, of course, isn't TLS profile compliant.

I assume someone is going to have to fix that as part of all the 5.0 TLS work anyway though?

> use plain HTTP for operator metrics

That's what we do for most components, and then add `kube-rbac-proxy` to export via HTTPS, so this ought to be easy / similar to other patches?

A prior post asking about `controllercmd` had no resolution other than to move anyway from using `controllercmd`. Looking at another openshift project using `controllercmd`, https://github.com/openshift/aws-ebs-csi-driver-operator/blob/master/cmd/aws-ebs-csi-driver-operator/main.go, it's not doing anything to use the centralized TLS profile.

Anyway, there is a way to configure the TLS settings in `controllercmd` although it requires duplicating some code from  `controllercmd`.  Another option is to convert to using controller runtime but that may be more work and we'd probably lose some functionality provided by `controllercmd`.

> 
> > use plain HTTP for operator metrics
> 
> That's what we do for most components, and then add `kube-rbac-proxy` to export via HTTPS, so this ought to be easy / similar to other patches?

I assume that would entail adding a `kube-rbac-proxy` sidecar container like https://github.com/openshift/ingress-node-firewall/blob/1c7880a7aa38192761538fb98446acca09509e09/config/manager/manager.yaml#L89. But then there's the issue of how to configure the values for the `--tls` params instead of hard-coding in the yaml which is even more problematic.
